status_semantics.FAIL: the claim does not survive; the registered consequence applies
status_semantics.INCONCLUSIVE: the design cannot answer it here
status_semantics.NOT_RUN: the arms or cells it needs are absent -- NOT a pass (§35.2)
status_semantics.MOOT: settled elsewhere; the contrast is not defined

broad_paper_condition: spec §10.1: the broad SPADE-method paper is supportable only if ALL of the seven conditions hold. If any fails the paper claim NARROWS -- it is never hidden

KF-1.claim: SPADE's certificate is valid prospectively under cross-fit
KF-1.fires_when: any primary F-CERT cell demonstrably below nominal after exact test + Holm
KF-1.sesoi_comparison: SESOI does not govern a containment proportion; the registered bar is the nominal alpha=0.8, and the worst confirmatory cell sits +0.0462 from it
KF-1.interpretation: no confirmatory cell is demonstrably below nominal across 44 cells. This is a failure to reject, not a proof of validity (§7.1) -- §22 measured what this design can and cannot detect

KF-2.claim: Certificate validity extends beyond hill d=6 sigma=0.25
KF-2.fires_when: C3/C4 INCONCLUSIVE or FAIL -> the claim narrows to hill
KF-2.sesoi_comparison: nominal alpha=0.8; SESOI does not apply
KF-2.interpretation: cross-family evidence is not clean, so the certificate claim narrows to hill and says so (§10.1 item 2). §37/§42 predicted SPADE would struggle off hill; a narrowing here is the registered outcome, not a surprise

KF-3.fires_when: m0 does not beat random_plate2 by >=SESOI on symmetric difference in any TARGET condition
KF-3.interpretation: targeted plate-2 SUR did not demonstrate value beyond random second-plate wells. Spec §7.3's registered consequence applies: the mechanistic claim comes out of the paper. This is THE load-bearing causal comparison of the study

KF-4.fires_when: m0 does not beat plate1_only on symmetric difference
KF-4.interpretation: plate 2 does not improve the map over plate 1 alone. Note the asymmetry spec §4.1 requires: plate1_only is budget-short by 8 wells, so it is a rounds/wells reference and NOT an equal-well comparator -- this failure is the stronger reading of the two, not the weaker one

KF-5.fires_when: the §7.5 conjunction is unmet -> trade-off, not an improvement
KF-5.interpretation: spade_cf_m4 does not meet the full §7.5 conjunction in hill-d6-s0.1, so m>0 is reported as a TRADE-OFF and not as an improvement. A regret reduction that damages the certificate is not a SPADE improvement

KF-6.claim: SPADE is competitive with Sobol on the map in TARGET regimes
KF-6.fires_when: sobol beats m0 by >SESOI in a TARGET condition
KF-6.interpretation: SPADE is within SESOI of Sobol on the symmetric difference in the TARGET regime, which is competitiveness and is never phrased as a win (§9 publication guard 1)

KF-7.claim: SPADE is competitive with qLogNEI on the map in TARGET regimes
KF-7.fires_when: qlognei beats m0 by >SESOI in a TARGET condition
KF-7.interpretation: SPADE is within SESOI of qLogNEI on the symmetric difference in the TARGET regime, which is competitiveness and is never phrased as a win (§9 publication guard 1)

KF-8.claim: Regret is at practical parity under a common terminal rule
KF-8.fires_when: m0 - best BO regret > SESOI under rule P
KF-8.interpretation: SPADE is within SESOI of qlognei under a common terminal rule. That is PARITY and §11 prohibits calling practical parity a superiority win -- §43.1 is this project doing it once already
KF-8.estimand_note: both sides are rule P. §43.1: the registered r* bar was a rule A column and the mixed comparison had to be withdrawn

KF-9.fires_when: any planned cell with tau >= tau_max reached the analysis
KF-9.sesoi_comparison: a count, not an effect size; SESOI does not apply
KF-9.interpretation: 4400 primary-gamma row(s) sit at or above the certifiability ceiling and reached the analyser. §4.5: no method certifies above tau_max at any budget, so these cells must be excluded BEFORE campaigns run. A zero scored there is a property of the threshold and reading it as a method failure is precisely the error the pre-run feasibility gate exists to stop. (Diagnostic gamma=0.99 rows are excluded from this check: spec names it a stress diagnostic never claimed as primary evidence, and Erratum 1 already registers that it may exceed the ceiling as a fact about noise and assurance, not a protocol breach.)

KF-10.claim: Empty-set degeneracy does not explain a pass
KF-10.fires_when: any PASS cell with empty rate > 0.50
KF-10.sesoi_comparison: empty-rate ceiling 50%; SESOI does not apply to a degeneracy guard
KF-10.interpretation: 8 cell(s) reached PASS on containment while certifying nothing in more than half their campaigns, and were downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE. §41.3 records the same failure mode off hill: the problem is emptiness, not miscoverage -- and an empty certificate is vacuously contained
